context.title: Tenants are protected for 48 hours after move-in, but the app doesn't help them use that time
context.body: HousingAnywhere holds a tenant's first month until 48 hours after the official move-in date. If the room isn't as described, the tenant can ask to cancel within that window and get a refund. It's a strong promise, but it lives in a help article. Move-in day is chaotic: tenants are often in a new country, the arrival time isn't always confirmed, and the 48 hours pass quickly. Reviews show tenants who reported problems inside the window and heard nothing, and others still chasing refunds.
assumptions: I haven't rented through HousingAnywhere. My view comes from the help centre, the Tenant Protection page, public reviews and the job posting, so the app may already do more than I can see.
Pausing the release while a report is open, and the 12-hour reply time, are proposals, not current policy. They'd need agreement with operations and finance.
The checklist items are examples; the real list would come from the most common reasons for cancel requests.
HousingAnywhere has no public design system, so the visual language comes from housinganywhere.com: deep teal-navy ink, slate text, an orange accent and Inter. No HousingAnywhere logo.
The tenant, landlord, room and amounts are fictional.

goals.title: Know what happens next
goals.body: Before move-in, show the confirmed time and exactly when the first payment is held and released.

goals.title: Use the 48 hours
goals.body: Turn the protection window into a short, guided room check on move-in day.

goals.title: Report with proof, stay protected
goals.body: Make reporting a problem one tap with photos, with the payment held and a clear reply time.

jtbd: When I move into a room I booked from abroad, I want to check it quickly and report anything wrong while I'm still protected, so I don't lose my first month or get stuck with a place that isn't as described.

evidence.step: Payment is held until 48h after move-in
evidence.finding: The first month's rent is charged at booking and held until 48 hours after the official move-in date, then released to the advertiser.

source.label: HousingAnywhere Help: Secure payment system for tenants

evidence.step: Problems must be reported inside 48 hours
evidence.finding: Within 48 hours of move-in, tenants can submit a 'Cancel Rental' request in the conversation with the advertiser if the room differs significantly from the listing. If approved, they get a full refund of the first month.

source.label: HousingAnywhere Help: Secure payment system for tenants

evidence.finding: HousingAnywhere markets Tenant Protection as a guarantee 'built into every rental', with landlord verification, scam monitoring and payment held until you move in.
HousingAnywhere has 3.2 out of 5 from 6,108 Trustpilot reviews: 54% five-star and 27% one-star.
Recent reviews describe a tenant who couldn't get an exact move-in time (Oct 2026), and another who reported problems 'all inside the 48-hour window' and got no reply (Oct 2026).
Reviewers say they're 'still struggling with the refund process' (Oct 2026) and that the Tenant Protection fee 'should be outlined clearer' (Sep 2026).

approaches: Explain Tenant Protection more clearly on the booking
Add a guided room checklist to the window
Make reporting a problem one tap, with photos
Show when the payment is held and released

ranges.title: Move-in Check
ranges.summary: Before move-in, a confirmed time and a payment timeline. On move-in day, a countdown with a short room checklist and a one-tap report with photos that keeps the payment held.
pros: Covers before, during and after the 48 hours.
Turns complaints into structured reports with evidence.
cons: Needs operations to commit to a reply time.
Pausing the release needs policy and finance sign-off.

decision.title: Move-in Check: make the 48 hours visible and usable
decision.body: Range 3. A payment timeline before move-in, a countdown and checklist on move-in day, and a one-tap report with photos that keeps the payment held and promises a reply time.
reasons: The reviews aren't about the rule, they're about not knowing what to do inside it, or not hearing back.
Structured reports with photos are faster for the support team to judge than a message thread.
A visible held payment is the clearest proof that Tenant Protection works.
decision.tradeoff: Pausing the release extends how long landlords wait. I'd limit it to reports with evidence, and show landlords the same status so they can fix issues quickly.

depth.body: Built in HousingAnywhere's visual language, running in an iPhone 17 frame. Three moments: before move-in, the confirmed move-in time from the landlord and a timeline of when the €650 first month is held and released; on move-in day, a 45-hour countdown and a five-item room check, with 'All good' enabled only once everything is ticked; when hot water fails, the report adds photos, pauses the release and promises a reply within 12 hours. Cards and the toast ease in quickly and turn off for people who reduce motion. The tenant, landlord and amounts are fictional.

validation.method: I'd start with cancel requests and support contacts raised in the first 48 hours, then test Move-in Check with tenants moving in during a busy intake week.
hypotheses: Tenants who use the checklist report real issues earlier and with clearer evidence.
Structured reports with photos are resolved faster than message-thread reports.
A visible payment timeline reduces 'where's my refund?' contacts.
